## Scope

`base` (`99cc3680`) → `HEAD` (`4d108b3b`) — one commit, *test(scripts): partition the quality-gate self-test into focusable families*. 2 files, +363/−4: `scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh` (+316, of which ~236 are genuinely new logic — registry, `verify_gate_family_partition`, `dispatch_gate_test_families`, `arm_suite_abort_trap`; the rest are family wrapper lines and comments) and `docs/notes/agent-quality-gate-mechanics.md` (+47). Untracked `.skill/` is my own review tooling, not part of the change — don't commit it.

**Verdict: passes.** No must-fix. Two follow-ups and one doc nit below.

The commit's central claim — *"Nothing moved… the diff is the wrapper lines only"* — is true, and I checked it mechanically rather than taking it on trust: stripping the 11 `run_*_family() {` / `} # end family:` lines and the 11 `arm_suite_abort_trap` calls from HEAD leaves a file that differs from `base` only by the new block, the new comments, and the replaced final `echo`. No test line was moved, reindented, or edited.

## Findings

**1. The suite can silently run zero tests — `scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:510-516` (verified)**

The awk `body == 2` rule permits *any* number of `dispatch_gate_test_families` lines after the closing marker, including none. Delete or relocate the single call at line 7476 and `verify_gate_family_partition` still passes, every family function is still defined, and the suite exits **0 with no output at all** — no "tests passed" line, nothing. I confirmed this: `bash /tmp/e.sh` with that one line removed → `exit=0`, empty output.

This is the exact failure mode the verifier exists to prevent, inverted. Before this change the tests ran unconditionally at top level and there was no single line whose loss disabled everything; the partition introduces that single point of failure and then doesn't check it. Consequence: a bad rebase or a careless edit turns the gate's own self-test into a no-op that reports green.

Smallest fix — count it in the awk and require exactly one:

```awk
body == 2 { ... if ($0 == "dispatch_gate_test_families") { dispatched++; next } ... }
END { ... if (dispatched != 1) { print "expected exactly one dispatch call" > "/dev/stderr"; exit 1 } }
```

*Follow-up, not blocking* — it needs a human edit to trigger, and that edit is visible in review.

**2. The documented invocation isn't in the repo's agent allowlist — `.claude/settings.json:31-32` (verified)**

`docs/notes/agent-quality-gate-mechanics.md:1119-1120` documents `GATE_TEST_FOCUS=routing-sources bash scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh`. The allowlist only carries `Bash(bash scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:*)` and the `./` variant; a Claude Code Bash rule matches on command prefix, and an env-var assignment in front defeats that. So the plain form runs unprompted and the documented focused form prompts — on exactly the agent machines the comment at `scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:597-598` says the feature is for.

The repo already has the convention for this: `.claude/settings.json:50` is `"Bash(ESLINT_BASELINE_MAIN=* node *)"`. Adding the parallel entry means touching `.claude/settings.json` **and** the pinned list in `scripts/context/check-settings-contract.mjs:74-75`, or `check-settings-contract` will red.

*Follow-up, not blocking.*

**3. Doc bullet overstates one case — `docs/notes/agent-quality-gate-mechanics.md:1139-1142`**

"`pnpm agent:quality-gate:test` … run[s] in that mode" (unfocused). It doesn't: `pnpm agent:quality-gate:test` is a bare `bash scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh` (`package.json:20`), so with `GATE_TEST_FOCUS` exported locally it runs focused. Only `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD` (the gate's mapped self-test) and `GITHUB_ACTIONS` (CI) force the refusal, which the *next* bullet states correctly. Drop `pnpm agent:quality-gate:test` from the first bullet's list.

*Preference.*

## Considered and cleared

- **The ERR-trap claim is correct, and I checked it rather than reasoning about it.** Setting the trap inside `arm_suite_abort_trap` does survive that helper's return — because bash only saves/restores the ERR trap on function entry when one is already set, and at `arm`'s entry it has just been reset by the family's own entry. Probed directly: the trap fires on a `false` inside a family, and `$LINENO` reports the absolute file line, so the diagnostic is byte-for-byte as useful as before. Helper functions, subshells and command substitutions still don't inherit it — identical to pre-change behaviour, and the stated reason for rejecting `set -E` holds.
- **Every family is self-contained** — this is what makes solo focus honest, and it's the thing most likely to be quietly wrong. Checked four ways: no variable assigned in one family is read by a later one; no column-0 `cd`, `export`, `set ±e` or `trap` at family scope; the shared real-repo fixtures (`.claude/skills/…tmp`, both `scripts/` symlink probes, `.codex/hooks.json`/`.claude/settings.json` copies, `turbo_facts_file`) are each created *and* torn down inside a single family; and every family writes `$output_file` before its first `assert_contains`. The three helpers now nested inside family bodies (`run_lockfile_scope_gate:1829`, `assert_hermetic_setup_routes:2670`, `run_parallel_interrupt_regression:5634`) are each called only from their own family, so defining them at family-call time is safe.
- **`verify_gate_family_partition` actually fires.** Four negative cases against modified copies, all caught with the right message and exit 1: a test appended after the dispatch call, a test between two families, a family missing from the registry, and definitions reordered against the registry. Deleting either marker is also caught.
- **The dispatch guards work.** Unknown family → exit 2 with the known set; whitespace-only focus → exit 2; `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` and `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD=…` each refuse with exit 2. `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD` is real and genuinely exported (`scripts/agent-quality-gate.sh:1143`) — the guard isn't watching a variable that never gets set.
- **Nothing external depended on what moved.** `"agent quality gate tests passed"` has no consumer anywhere in the repo. The gate's own handling of the self-test command is untouched on all four surfaces: `command_dedupe_key:2067`, `is_stamp_exempt_command:5224`, the serialization case at `5462`, and `implementation_signature:4671`. `scripts/repo-health/file-size-watchlist.test.mjs:273` already exempts this file, so +316 lines won't trip the size watchlist.
- **Formatting and lint.** `bash -n` clean; shellcheck 0.11.0 (the pinned version) gives *byte-identical* output on base and HEAD — one pre-existing SC1091. `shfmt` is not among trunk's enabled linters, so the deliberately un-reindented bodies are safe. The new markdown table is correctly prettier-shaped (every column padded to longest-content+2; my first read said otherwise, which was an artifact of byte-vs-character counting on the em-dashes). `git diff --check` clean, no tabs, no trailing whitespace, no conflict markers, no secrets.
- **Sibling convention.** `scripts/agent-autoreview.test.sh` has a prior art focus mechanism (`AUTOREVIEW_TEST_FOCUS` + `verify_canonical_family_partition:8425`), but it partitions *named regression functions* into families — structurally inapplicable to a flat statement suite. The gate's adaptation doesn't drift from anything it should be mirroring. Worth knowing that the sibling prints a `rerun="AUTOREVIEW_TEST_FOCUS=… bash …"` hint on family failure; the gate suite gives you a line number but not which family died. Nice-to-have, not a defect.

## What I could not do

**I never ran a single test.** `node_modules` is absent in this checkout — `pnpm install` has not run here — so `GATE_TEST_FOCUS=gate-contract` dies within a second on `Cannot find package 'js-yaml'` from `scripts/gate/lockfile-scope.mjs`. I did not install dependencies, since that's a side effect you didn't ask for. Everything above about the partition machinery is direct evidence (it all executes before the first test), but everything about the *tests* is static analysis only.

Concretely unverified: that any family passes solo; that the unfocused run still passes; and the doc's runtime table (2s → 319s per family, "~9-minute suite"). The table is self-consistent — the solo runtimes sum to ~696s, more than the ~540s full run, which the in-process `run_gate` output cache explains — but I measured none of it.

**No second-model pass.** `~/.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview` isn't installed on this machine, and the repo-local `pnpm agent:autoreview` adapter needs the same missing `node_modules`; this session is also instructed not to spawn subagents unasked. So this is a single-model read, and the class of defect that channel is best at — a rule that moved without landing anywhere — is the class least covered here.

## Proof still owed

Reading source established the structure, not that the software runs. Before merge: `pnpm install`, then `bash scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh` unfocused and confirm it prints `agent quality gate tests passed` — and one solo `GATE_TEST_FOCUS=<family>` run per family, which is the only thing that turns my static self-containment argument into a fact and substantiates the runtime table. This is separate from whatever the pre-push gate itself requires; note that touching this file busts every fresh-run stamp via `implementation_signature`, so the next gate run will be a full one.

The focus guard can allow a partial self-test inside a documented full-gate mode. The structural verifier can also return success when no family dispatch exists.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Refuse focus for lockless full-gate runs — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1995-4d108b3b9c42/scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:600-603
  When a developer exports `GATE_TEST_FOCUS` and runs the full gate with the documented `--no-lock` or `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK=0` escape hatch, the gate does not export `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD`. Outside GitHub Actions, this check therefore accepts the focus, and the mapped self-test can return success after one family and let the full gate record partial validation as complete. Clear the focus in full-suite callers or use an explicit focused-run marker instead of lock ownership. See `docs/notes/agent-quality-gate-mechanics.md:594-598`.

- [P2] Require exactly one dispatch after the partition — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1995-4d108b3b9c42/scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:510-515
  If the final `dispatch_gate_test_families` line is deleted during a later edit or merge, this verifier accepts zero dispatches. Bash then reaches EOF after defining the family functions and exits 0 without running any test. I reproduced this with a source copy, which returned status 0 with no output. Count dispatch occurrences and fail unless there is exactly one.
